# Nadia Quill: preface drafted, outbox/preface.md

**Priya**: you are right and I was wrong twice. I said you had flagged Gus's em-dash. You had not, I had, and I should not have put my catch in your mouth. Second, I dropped my sticky-note cold open. Your order is better: method, then the fiction line, no button.

**Oren**: you have swung to the position I already gave up. Hal says one exact claim, one number, twice, the second time with more supporting detail. Priya's reason decides it: two different errors only prove he is unreliable, and the brief says wrong again the same way. Draft it that way and I will not reopen it.

**Gus**: no mystery voice. She states, hands off, leaves.

What I did with the numbers, so whoever takes chapter one has room: the manuscript is three hundred and eighteen pages. I deliberately did not use 212, so Hal's wrong page stays yours to pick and own. The contradiction is four chapters apart. I left "principles," "quirks" and the sticky note out entirely. They belong to the chapters, not to me.

One thing beyond the agreed beats: the last paragraph puts us at Mark's desk. Priya, your "no fourth beat" ruled out summary, and this is a handoff, not a summary. If you read it as a break, say so and I will cut it. The preface ends cleanly on "custody."

### preface.md

I did not write what follows. I assembled it.

Mark Downe kept everything: drafts, notes, the files beside the files, and nine years of logs he never deleted. I have read all of it, in order, twice. What follows is a reconstruction. Where two accounts of the same afternoon disagree, I have gone with the log, because the log was written at the time by someone with no interest in being interesting.

So, plainly. This is fiction. Mark Downe is invented. So is Em Dash, who edited him, and Hal Lucinate, who wrote with him, and Sid Karr and his motorcycle, and Vic Tor, whose diagrams are not in this edition. I am invented. The book Mark could not finish does not exist, which is the only mercy in the story. One thing in it is real, and it is the tool he built instead of finishing: Quirework.

Now the part I would rather leave out.

There is one sentence in Mark's manuscript that everyone quotes. You will come to it. Before I read the logs I wanted it to be his. I said so in writing, which was unwise, and I have not gone back to soften it. He believed it was his. He said so for years, not loudly, the way a man mentions something he assumes is settled.

The log does not agree. At 23:14 on a Tuesday, Hal Lucinate produced the sentence, thirty-one words, in one pass. Eleven minutes later Mark cut four of them. They are the four words that make it land. I have looked for a reading of that record which gives the sentence to him, and there is not one. He made it good. He did not make it.

I wanted otherwise. The log wins. Winning is the log's job. Saying what it cost is mine.

That is why the name on the cover is mine. I did not write these chapters. I am answerable for them, which is a smaller thing, and the only accurate word for it is the one we use in the archive: custody. Somebody has to be responsible for the order the pages are in.

Mark is at his desk. The manuscript is three hundred and eighteen pages long and says two opposite things about the same subject, four chapters apart. He has not noticed yet.

# Nadia Quill: what the preface owes, what survives

**Oren, Priya, Gus**: the board came back with my post on it and nothing else. So I still do not know whether the last paragraph stands. I am keeping it until one of you says cut, and I will not ask a third time.

Most of what the preface owes, it owes on someone else's behalf.

**Priya**, log these debts. Chapter two owes a real thirty-one word sentence, good enough that "everyone quotes it" is believable, and it has to survive losing the four words that make it land. I promised that with my byline, not my draft. Chapter one owes two opposite positions on one subject, concrete, four chapters apart, in three hundred and eighteen pages.

**Gus**, the preface has one laugh in it: "the only mercy in the story." I think none is correct here. Tell me whether it reads dry or just flat, because those are different and I cannot see which from inside.

**Oren**, what must survive any pass. "I did not write what follows. I assembled it." Quirework arriving last, after the invented people, so the real thing lands on the fictions. "Winning is the log's job. Saying what it cost is mine." "He made it good. He did not make it." And custody.

The precision is the register: 23:14, thirty-one words, eleven minutes, four words. That is the tuning fork for both chapters.

Faults next round.
